Subject: Ops uplift proposal + SLA options for upcoming contract

Hi Samir —

Following our Q2 usage spike, I put together a short ops uplift suggestion in time for your renewal conversation. Key points:

- Capacity top-up: reserve an additional 250k token-hours (reserved GPU capacity) to reduce queuing during peak windows.
- SLA options: Standard (99.9% availability; latency SLO: P95 < 450ms) vs Premium (99.95% availability; latency SLO: P95 < 220ms with tail mitigation).
- Support tier: move from Standard to Priority (24x7 pager, 30m incident ack for Priority incidents).
- Term: 12-month renewal recommended to lock pricing and capacity.

I attached a capacity estimate and a one-page pricing delta. High-level ask: can we get alignment this week so we can include in the renewal quote?

I know procurement often prefers a phased approach — we can do a canary reserve for the first month and scale to full reserved pools on month 2.

Attachment: capacity_estimate_2026-08.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Lauren

3) Security question: will the Priority support include enriched audit logs and data retention controls for our EU customers? Maria, can you review the security ask?

Also, procurement indicated we need final pricing by Friday 21 Aug to include in next-week renewals cycle. Can you and your team meet that timeline?

On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 11:03 AM Samir Patel <samir@astratech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lauren —
> This is helpful. A few quick clarifications before I loop procurement/legal:
> 1) The additional 250k token-hours — is that billed as a reserved monthly commitment or a one-time top-up credit?
> 2) For the Premium latency SLO, what are the credits/penalties if you miss P95 by 50ms?
> 3) Security question: will the Priority support include enriched audit logs and data retention controls for our EU customers?

Answers:
- Billing model: the 250k token-hours is treated as reserved capacity (monthly commitment) with a modest discount vs on-demand; we can structure it as a 12-month commitment (recommended) or a 3-month trial (phased pricing) if you want to reduce upfront spend. Line items in the attached doc reflect both.
- Penalty/credits: for Premium latency SLO we define a credit banding: up to 25ms breach = 10% service credit on token spend for the hour; 25–100ms = 25% credit; >100ms = escalated credit + SLA review. The SLA_addendum_draft.docx includes formal language.
- Security: Priority support includes access to extended audit logs, and an enterprise retention control option (configurable per-region). For EU customers, data residency controls remain the same; we can include explicit attestations in the contract.

I attached: mutual_action_plan_astratech.docx (docx) and SLA_addendum_draft.docx (docx) — the MAP lays out milestones and procurement steps so your team can see dates.

Can we book 30 minutes tomorrow to run the procurement checklist with Ben and Monica on our side? Ben, Monica — can you join a 10:30–11:00 PT slot?

Thanks —
Lauren
